quotes_checked: all 31 distinct verses on the card checked against the Berean; every quote is exact (the clause and first-sentence excerpts match the verse text; Mark 12:30's stray mark omitted as the notes say)

fixes.why: 'The image of God is marred and remains' is not what Lutheran confession says (the Formula of Concord speaks of the image as lost in its righteousness) nor what Reformed writers say (image lost in the narrow sense, remaining in the wide sense). A Lutheran or Reformed reader would not sign the single word 'marred'. The causal 'which is why' also states the holders' reasoning as the text's.
fixes.fix: Replace with: "Lutheran and Reformed readers speak of the image as lost in the righteousness, holiness and true knowledge it first had and as remaining in the dignity of the person, in their own differing words; Genesis 9:6 and James 3:9 are cited for the second."

fixes.why: Ephesians 4:24 and Colossians 3:10 are the verses Reformed and Lutheran holders cite first for what the image consisted of and what is renewed in Christ. They sit only in reading 1, and reading 2 has no verse from the Genesis fall itself. Genesis 2:17 and 3:19 are the text on which every reading's account of death rests.
fixes.fix: Add to reading 2: Ephesians 4:24 ("and to put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness.") note "Read as naming what the image consisted of and what Christ renews." And add Genesis 3:19 ("For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.") note "The sentence of death on Adam, read as passing to his descendants." Drop Job 14:4 or Genesis 5:3 if the count must stay at 7.

fixes.why: The Genesis fall is not cited, though Catholic and Orthodox readings of death and corruption rest on it (Genesis 3:19), and the image taken up in Christ (1 Corinthians 15:49) is central to the growth into likeness this reading describes.
fixes.fix: Add 1 Corinthians 15:49 ("And just as we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man.") note "Read as the likeness the believer grows into: the heavenly man's." Replace Colossians 3:10 if the count must stay at 7, since reading 2 now carries Ephesians 4:24.

fixes.why: The label begins 'One living person ... each person answers for his or her own sin'. The summary itself says Wesleyans hold the inherited corruption of reading 2, and Wesleyan anthropology is not a single whole-person view, so a Wesleyan would not own this label. Naming them in held_by for it reads as placing them in a reading they would not sign. The sentence on Eastern Orthodox readers sits in a reading they are not credited with.
fixes.fix: Set reading 3 held_by to ["Anabaptist", "Baptist / free church"]. Move 'hold also that Christ's work covers children' into reading 2's summary after 'their members differ in how they state the guilt'. Delete the Eastern Orthodox sentence from reading 3's summary (it is already in reading 1).

fixes.why: The reading bundles three-part language with the fall as the death of the spirit. Pentecostal and Charismatic members commonly pair three-part language with the Wesleyan or Baptist account of the fall, and many are two-part, as the sentence about 'several other traditions' implies only vaguely.
fixes.fix: After 'Pentecostal and Charismatic readers commonly speak this way' add: "though their members hold a range of accounts of the fall and of how many parts a person has."

fixes.why: The summary names the new birth and the Spirit's witness with the believer's spirit, and the fall as the death of the spirit toward God, but cites no verse for any of these except Ephesians 2:1. Holders cite John 3:6 and Romans 8:16 first, and Genesis 2:17 for the fall.
fixes.fix: Add Romans 8:16 ("The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God's children.") note "The Spirit and the believer's spirit named together."; John 3:6 ("Flesh is born of flesh, but spirit is born of the Spirit.") note "Read as the spirit made alive in the new birth."; Genesis 2:17 ("for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.") note "Read as a death toward God that came on the day of the fall." Drop Luke 1:47 and 1 Corinthians 2:14 if the count must stay at 7.

fixes.why: The Berean reads 'your spirit is alive', but the Greek has no 'your': it says 'the spirit [is] life because of righteousness', and many take 'the spirit' as the Holy Spirit. The note rests on the Berean's choice of word, which the original does not require.
fixes.fix: Note: "Read as the believer's spirit alive through Christ's presence; the Greek says only 'the spirit', and other readers take it as the Holy Spirit."

fixes.where: reading 4 passage 1 Corinthians 2:14 and reading 3 passage 1 Corinthians 15:44
fixes.why: 'Natural' in both verses is the Greek psychikos, 'soul-ish', set against pneumatikos, 'spirit-ish'. The English hides the soul/spirit contrast on which both readings lean.
fixes.fix: Add to both notes: "The Greek word for 'natural' is psychikos, formed from psyche, 'soul'."

fixes.why: The writer asked whether Ephesians 2:1 needs an answer outside reading 4. It does: it is the one verse of reading 4 the others have not been given a way to take, while reading 4's answers cover their main verses. Without it the card leaves its own cited verse unanswered by three of four readings.
fixes.fix: Reading 1 answers: "They take 'dead in trespasses' as separation from God's life that Christ restores, applied to the whole person." Reading 2: "They take Ephesians 2:1 with 2:3 as the whole person dead in trespasses and by nature children of wrath." Reading 3: "They take 'dead in your trespasses' as the death that sin brings to the person who sins, as in Romans 7:9, and not the death of one part."

fixes.why: Readings 1 to 3 each answer the other readings' main verses; reading 4 answers only the verses on parts. Romans 5:12 and Psalm 51:5 are the other readings' central fall verses and nothing is said of how this reading takes them.
fixes.fix: Add: "Holders of this reading who hold the fall as in reading 2 or 3 take Romans 5, Psalm 51:5 and Ezekiel 18:20 as those readings do; this reading adds an account of what part of a person the fall touched."

fixes.why: The card says the English words render nephesh and ruach with wider senses but not the fact the readings most turn on: the Hebrew phrase translated 'living being' in Genesis 2:7 is used in Genesis 1 of the animals (Berean 'living creatures', 1:24). Stating that is neutral and original-based; it does not favour a reading.
fixes.fix: Append: "The Hebrew phrase translated 'living being' in Genesis 2:7 is the one the Berean renders 'living creatures' of the animals in Genesis 1:24; readers differ on what that shows."

fixes.why: Romans 5:12 is the hinge of readings 1 to 3, and its last Greek words (eph' ho) are translated differently: 'because', 'in whom' (the old Latin reading), 'with the result that'. A reader should know the Berean's 'because all sinned' is one rendering. Per the original-arbitrates rule this is the original's own openness, stated without a verdict.
fixes.fix: Add term {"term": "because all sinned", "note": "The Greek words eph' ho at the end of Romans 5:12 have been rendered 'because', 'in whom' and 'with the result that'; readers differ partly on this, and the Berean's 'because' is one of the renderings."}

fixes.where: reading 3 passage Ezekiel 18:20 and reading 2 passages Psalm 51:5, Job 14:4
fixes.why: Ezekiel 18 answers a proverb about exile in Israel, and Psalm 51 and Job 14 are a poet's and a sufferer's words. Their notes say 'Read as', which is right for Psalm 51 and Job, but the Ezekiel note states 'Each person answers for his own sin' as the verse's own claim in the later Christian debate.
fixes.fix: Ezekiel 18:20 note: "Read by holders of this reading as saying each person answers for his own sin."

fixes.why: The image is treated in the card as what a person has or is, though the Genesis text and the New Testament also give it as a calling and as fulfilled in Christ (Colossians 1:15, 1 Corinthians 15:49). All four readings take Christ as the image of God, so this belongs in the common ground without choosing among them.
fixes.fix: Add to the agreed passages Colossians 1:15 ("The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation.") and to agreed.summary after the 'very good' sentence: "The text also calls Christ the image of God." Remove Genesis 1:31 from the agreed passages if the count must stay at 7.

summary: Every quote is the Berean's exact words, and no verdict wording turned up, but the Lutheran and Reformed account of the image is stated in a way they would not sign, and Wesleyans are credited with a reading whose label they would not own. Each reading also lacks first-cited verses and some answers (Genesis 3:19 and 2:17, Ephesians 4:24, John 3:6, Romans 8:16, an answer to Ephesians 2:1), and two Berean renderings (Romans 8:10, psychikos) and the eph' ho of Romans 5:12 hide what the original leaves open.
